title: Mohenjo-daro

place.label: Mohenjo-daro, Larkana District, Sindh, Pakistan
place.basis: official UNESCO World Heritage point; not a boundary
place.coords_source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre official point for Archaeological Ruins at Moenjodaro (World Heritage List 138), published as N27 19 45 E68 8 20 at https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/138/maps/ (table read 2026-11-27); approximate, not a boundary

tiers.everyday: Mohenjo-daro in Pakistan was a large planned city of the Indus civilization, with straight streets, baked-brick houses and covered drains, more than 4,000 years ago.
tiers.student: UNESCO describes Mohenjo-daro as South Asia's most intact city site, from the early third millennium BC, and as the Indus civilisation's main metropolis, which flourished about 2500-1500 BC. Streets cross at right angles and it has a drainage system, wells and public baths. The ruins were found in 1922 and inscribed in 1980.

timeline.event: The city dates from the early third millennium BC
